subject: environmental-science
title: Impact Prediction Methods
welcome_lead: Matrices, networks, GIS overlays — toolkits to forecast environmental change.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on impact prediction techniques.
final_note: Every prediction carries uncertainty — communicate it transparently.

concepts.def: Grid cross-referencing project actions vs environmental components.
Shows causal chains of direct and indirect impacts.
GIS layering to identify spatial conflicts (McHarg's Design with Nature).
Combined effect of past, present and reasonably foreseeable activities.
Importance of an impact based on magnitude, duration, reversibility and receptor sensitivity.
Stakeholder engagement required by EIA Directive Article 6.

walkthroughs.body_html: Leopold matrices use 8800 cells (100 actions × 88 components). Cells score magnitude and importance.
Network diagrams reveal cascading impacts — e.g., road → noise → wildlife displacement → ecotourism revenue.
Ian McHarg's overlay technique (1969) underlies modern GIS suitability analysis for site selection.
